title: Missionaries are paired and sent, and their families must be supported
setting: A general conference met at Amherst, Ohio, on 25 January 1832, about fifty miles west of Kirtland. William McLellin later said seventy to eighty church officers attended. Joseph Smith was ordained President of the High Priesthood there. Elders who had offered to preach asked to know the Lord’s will for them. Joseph dictated two revelations that day, now verses 1–22 and 23–36. The 1835 Doctrine and Covenants combined them into one section.
summary: The first revelation tells those who volunteered to preach to go without delay and labor with their might. Faithful workers are promised sheaves, honor, and eternal life. William McLellin’s eastern mission is revoked; he is chastened for murmuring, forgiven, and sent south with Luke Johnson. Orson Hyde, Samuel Smith, Lyman Johnson, and Orson Pratt go east, and other pairs go west and south. Houses that reject them are to be left with the dust shaken off as a testimony. The second revelation asks the church to support the families of those sent out. A man who must provide for his own family may stay and keep his crown, but idlers have no place. It ends by pairing fourteen more men, including Hyrum Smith, Reynolds Cahoon, and Ezra Thayre.

contextNote.title: Two duties that need not compete
contextNote.text: Many elders who volunteered had families who depended on them. Verse 24 makes the support of those families a duty of the church. Verse 25 asks the elders to find places for their families where members are willing. Verse 26 then says those with such support must not fail to go. Verse 28 says the man who must provide for his family “shall in nowise lose his crown” by staying. Verse 29 marks the limit, since the idler has no place in the church. In this passage, providing for a family counts as faithful labor, not as a lesser calling.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 71–75 includes these mission calls and their care for families. What do verses 24–28 ask of the church, of the missionaries, and of fathers who stay home?

reviewNote: Read all 36 verses. Official heading gives Amherst, 25 January 1832, two revelations (vv. 1–22, 23–36), and Joseph’s ordination as President of the High Priesthood.
